record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.context_brief: covering number for approximate root selection
record.original_question: For the same 6-dimensional family of real polynomial systems f_a(x,y)=x^2-y^2+a(x,y), g_b(x,y)=xy+b(x,y) with a and b of degree at most 1, what is the corresponding covering-number problem for approximate solution selectors: the continuous map on each open set may choose a point that is merely within a fixed positive ε-neighborhood of some actual root rather than being an exact root?

evidence.quote:
Problem 2B. The same questions concerning the approximate solu-
tions. That is, for any i and (a, b) ∈ Ui the value ϕi(a, b) should be not
necessarily a root of (fa, gb), but just a point in the ε–neighborhood of
such a root for some ﬁxed positive ε.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the 6-dimensional real parameter space P consisting of pairs (a,b) where a(x,y) and b(x,y) are real polynomials in two variables of degree at most 1, i.e. a(x,y) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 y and b(x,y) = b_0 + b_1 x + b_2 y. For each (a,b) ∈ P, define the polynomial system

  f_{a}(x,y) = x^2 - y^2 + a(x,y),
  g_{b}(x,y) = xy + b(x,y),

and let R(a,b) ⊂ R^2 denote the (finite, generically) set of common real roots of f_a and g_b.

Fix a real number ε > 0. An ε-approximate continuous root selector over an open set U ⊂ P is a continuous map φ : U → R^2 such that for every (a,b) ∈ U there exists p ∈ R(a,b) with ‖φ(a,b) − p‖ < ε.

Define the ε-approximate covering number N(ε) of the family {(f_a, g_b) : (a,b) ∈ P} to be the smallest positive integer N such that there exists an open cover P = U_1 ∪ U_2 ∪ ⋯ ∪ U_N together with continuous ε-approximate root selectors φ_i : U_i → R^2 for each i = 1,…,N.

Determine N(ε) (in particular, its dependence on ε for sufficiently small ε > 0), or determine sharp upper and lower bounds for N(ε).
artifact.status_search_result: No published solution to this approximate-root covering-number problem for the specified family of degree-≤2 real polynomial systems was located. The problem appears to remain open.
